title: Hygge the secret to a happy winter
titleChinese: 享受快乐冬天的秘密是什么？
paragraphs: Imagine this scene: it's blowing a gale outside, you're snuggled up on the sofa under a warm duvet, chatting and reminiscing with your closest friends.

That content, snug feeling has a name in Danish - 'hygge'. And, as Denmark recently won the title of 'happiest country in the world', the rest of the world is becoming more and more interested in finding ways to embrace this concept.

'Hygge' - originally from a Norwegian word meaning 'wellbeing' - doesn't have an exact equivalent in English. It's often translated as cosiness, or as blogger Anna West told the BBC, "cosiness of the soul." But, as translator ToveMaren Stakkestad explains: "Hygge was never meant to be translated. It was meant to be felt."

Essentially, Hygge involves creating a warm, cosy atmosphere and enjoying it with your loved ones. Danish winters are long and dark and so achieving 'hygge' is particularly relevant during this season. A typical 'hygge' activity during winter could be, enjoying delicious homemade food and light-hearted conversation with friends - preferably in the warm glow of candlelight; or maybe sipping a glass of mulled wine in the hot tub after a day spent skiing.

However, Hygge isn't only confined to the bleak winter months - it can also describe that warm, fuzzy feeling you get after a walk through a forest with friends on summer's day or a family barbecue in the park.

The concept of 'hygge' is currently taking the world by storm with more and more people becoming obsessed with achieving a state of wellbeing. Articles, books and stocking fillers, full of tips on how to achieve hygge, are hitting the market. Although, some believe this has become a marketing and advertising ploy, the benefits of staying happy cannot be underestimated. So, as the winter nights draw in, instead of hibernating, get into your favourite onesie, bake some cookies and curl up by a roaring fire with a good book. And if you can do this with friends and family, even better — hygge is meant to be shared.

vocabulary.entry: gale [n.] /ɡeɪl/ 大风；狂风
vocabulary.example: The gale blew down several trees.
vocabulary.translation: 大风吹倒了几棵树。

vocabulary.entry: snuggled up [phr.] /ˈsnʌɡəld ʌp/ 依偎；蜷伏 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The children snuggled up under the blanket.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们在毯子下依偎在一起。

vocabulary.entry: reminisce [v.] /ˌremɪˈnɪs/ 追忆往事；回忆
vocabulary.example: They sat around reminiscing about their school days.
vocabulary.translation: 他们围坐在一起追忆学生时代。

vocabulary.entry: snug [adj.] /snʌɡ/ 舒适的；温暖的
vocabulary.example: The cabin was small but snug.
vocabulary.translation: 小屋虽小但很舒适。

vocabulary.entry: cosy [adj.] /ˈkəʊzi/ 舒适的；惬意的 (英式拼写，美式: cozy)
vocabulary.example: We had a cosy evening by the fire.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在炉火旁度过了一个舒适的夜晚。

vocabulary.entry: mulled wine [n.] /mʌld waɪn/ 热葡萄酒
vocabulary.example: Mulled wine is popular at Christmas markets.
vocabulary.translation: 热葡萄酒在圣诞市场上很受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: fuzzy [adj.] /ˈfʌzi/ 温暖惬意的；模糊的
vocabulary.example: I had a warm fuzzy feeling after the meal.
vocabulary.translation: 饭后我有一种温暖惬意的感觉。

vocabulary.entry: obsessed with [phr.] /əbˈsest wɪð/ 痴迷于 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He is obsessed with video games.
vocabulary.translation: 他痴迷于电子游戏。

vocabulary.entry: ploy [n.] /plɔɪ/ 策略；花招
vocabulary.example: The offer was just a marketing ploy.
vocabulary.translation: 这个优惠只是一个营销策略。

vocabulary.entry: onesie [n.] /ˈwʌnzi/ 连体衣；连身睡衣 (口语)
vocabulary.example: She wore a fluffy onesie at home.
vocabulary.translation: 她在家穿着毛绒连体衣。

vocabulary.entry: take...by storm [phr.] /teɪk baɪ stɔːm/ 风靡；使大为轰动 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The new singer took the charts by storm.
vocabulary.translation: 这位新歌手在排行榜上大受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: be confined to [phr.] /biː kənˈfaɪnd tuː/ 局限于 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The problem is not confined to one region.
vocabulary.translation: 这个问题不局限于一个地区。

vocabulary.entry: draw in [phr.] /drɔː ɪn/ （白昼）渐短；(天黑)渐早
vocabulary.example: As winter approaches, the evenings draw in.
vocabulary.translation: 随着冬天的临近，夜晚来得更早了。

vocabulary.entry: hibernate [v.] /ˈhaɪbəneɪt/ 冬眠；蛰伏
vocabulary.example: Bears hibernate during the winter.
vocabulary.translation: 熊在冬天冬眠。

vocabulary.entry: curl up [phr.] /kɜːl ʌp/ 蜷缩；蜷伏
vocabulary.example: She curled up on the sofa with a book.
vocabulary.translation: 她蜷缩在沙发上看书。

vocabulary.entry: wellbeing [n.] /ˌwelˈbiːɪŋ/ 幸福；健康
vocabulary.example: Exercise is important for mental wellbeing.
vocabulary.translation: 锻炼对心理健康很重要。

vocabulary.entry: equivalent [n.] /ɪˈkwɪvələnt/ 对等的人（或事物）
vocabulary.example: There is no English equivalent for this word.
vocabulary.translation: 这个词在英语中没有对等词。

vocabulary.entry: light-hearted [adj.] /ˌlaɪt ˈhɑːtɪd/ 轻松愉快的
vocabulary.example: The conversation was light-hearted and fun.
vocabulary.translation: 谈话轻松愉快。

vocabulary.entry: preferably [adv.] /ˈprefərəbli/ 最好是；更可取地
vocabulary.example: Bring your own lunch, preferably something healthy.
vocabulary.translation: 自带午餐，最好是健康的东西。

vocabulary.entry: underestimate [v.] /ˌʌndərˈestɪmeɪt/ 低估
vocabulary.example: Don't underestimate the power of a kind word.
vocabulary.translation: 不要低估一句好话的力量。
